description: Error and usage output is printed with the regular print functions, and PrintErrln and PrintErrf themselves delegate to the regular output.

provenance.construction: reverse of 40d34bca1b: the new side of the diff is the code before the change

expected.rationale: Error text written to the normal output writer breaks callers that capture or redirect stderr and makes SetErr ineffective, as the linked issue reports. Nothing crashes and no data is lost, so the risk is LOW. This level is a judgement, not an advisory rating.

issues.description: PrintErrln and PrintErrf are implemented with Print, so output meant for the error stream goes to the normal output stream.
Errors and the usage hint are printed with Println and Printf to the regular output writer, so SetErr and stderr never receive them.
